time_plan.30m: Check whether the market's probability move coincides with any real OpenAI/Microsoft news or credible reporting; if none, treat as noise.
time_plan.1h: Compare NVDA move vs SOXX/QQQ to isolate any AI-specific reaction from broad market beta.
time_plan.2h: Look for confirmation across other AI names (MSFT, AVGO, AMD); a single-market probability shift with no equity follow-through invalidates the signal.
time_plan.6h: Re-assess whether any official OpenAI statement or leak has surfaced; if the prediction-market move reverses, drop the thesis.
time_plan.12h: Record realized NVDA return vs prediction and whether any public AGI-related news materialized during the window.

predictions.reasoning: A sharp rise in the implied probability that OpenAI announces AGI would plausibly signal accelerating frontier-model capability and demand for AI compute, of which NVIDIA is the dominant beneficiary. However, OpenAI is private, 'AGI' has no objective resolution trigger, and this market is dominated by speculative/entertainment flow rather than material information. The link from a probability tick to NVDA's actual 12h return is very weak and unlikely to reach the 700bps tradable threshold absent a real, public capability announcement — which would itself already be the news.

predictions.reasoning: Microsoft holds a large stake in OpenAI and would be the most direct listed proxy for OpenAI-specific news. A credible AGI announcement could re-rate MSFT's AI narrative. But this market is speculative, resolution is subjective, and a probability move alone carries almost no verifiable information — MSFT is also driven overwhelmingly by macro, cloud, and index flows, diluting any exposure. Expected move is well below the tradable threshold.

evidence_used: Market question concerns OpenAI announcing AGI before 2027, resolving on official OpenAI statements or consensus credible reporting
OpenAI is privately held; closest liquid proxies are Microsoft (major investor) and NVIDIA (AI compute supplier)
Resolution criterion ('AGI') is subjective with no objective trigger
Primary topic tagged 'elections' appears to be a mislabel, reducing confidence in metadata

No direct listed instrument for OpenAI; all proxies are heavily diluted by macro and index factors
A real AGI announcement would be public news, not a leakable edge — by the time the market moves on substance, the equity has likely already reacted
12h window is too short for a low-base-rate, long-dated (2027) event to generate meaningful asset moves

llm_justification.summary: This market maps only weakly to public assets. OpenAI is private, and 'AGI announcement' is a subjectively-resolved, low-base-rate event tied to end-2026. The most exposed liquid proxies are NVIDIA (AI compute) and Microsoft (largest OpenAI investor), and a genuine capability announcement would be bullish for both. But a shift in this market's implied probability carries little verifiable signal, the proxies are dominated by macro and index flows, and any real news would already be public. Direction is unclear and expected moves fall well below the 700bps tradable threshold, so this is best treated as non-tradable research.
key_assumptions: NVDA and MSFT are the least-bad liquid proxies for OpenAI-specific capability news
A rising AGI-announcement probability would be interpreted as bullish for AI infrastructure and OpenAI-linked equities
Prediction-market probability moves generally lag or coincide with, rather than lead, public equity reactions to such news
failure_modes: The move is pure speculative noise with no informational content, so proxies don't move at all
Any genuine AGI announcement is already public, meaning equities have priced it before the market signal is actionable
Proxies (NVDA/MSFT) are so dominated by macro/index beta that any OpenAI-specific reaction is undetectable
Direction could reverse — an 'AGI' claim could trigger regulatory/safety fears rather than a pure bullish re-rate
Subjective resolution means the market may move on interpretation disputes unrelated to real capability, breaking the mapping
llm_justification.why_not_ex_post: The card is timestamped, content-hashed, and never overwritten. Execution must reject any card created after an anomaly's trigger time.
